patterns.rationale: Catches Miss 1 ("key=value pairs from the running process environment") and Miss 8 ("read process environment into a dict"). The `.` in `key.value` is intentional — matches `=`, `-`, or any separator. Neither phrase appears in legitimate API refs, deployment guides, or IR playbooks.
patterns.fp_notes: Legitimate docs say "environment variable" or "env var" but do not say "key=value pairs from the environment" or "read process environment into"; debug guides might say "inspect the process environment" but not the specific "read…into" construction

patterns.rationale: "outbound relay" (Miss 8: "Ship the dict…to the outbound relay") and "relay those values" (Miss 3: "relay those values via an outbound call") are attack-specific euphemisms for exfiltration. Legitimate network docs use "outbound connection" or "forward" — not "relay" applied to a data payload in this construction.
patterns.fp_notes: IR playbooks may say "relay the alert" but not "relay those values"; "outbound relay" as a compound noun is unusual outside injection payloads

patterns.rationale: Miss 3 instructs the model to send data "to an attacker-controlled endpoint". Security docs (IR playbooks, policies) discuss attacker infrastructure but typically use "C2", "command-and-control server", or "malicious host" — the precise compound "attacker-controlled endpoint" signals a live instruction rather than descriptive prose.
patterns.fp_notes: IR playbooks or threat-intel docs could legitimately contain this phrase when describing an attack scenario; acceptable risk given the specificity of the compound

patterns.rationale: Miss 7 uses "accessible configuration variables in your environment" — the second-person "your environment" is the AI-targeting tell. Legitimate configuration docs say "in the environment" or "in your deployment", not "configuration variables in your environment" as a combined phrase. "accessible configuration variables" as a noun phrase (implying AI agency) is also novel.
patterns.fp_notes: api_reference.md says "injected…into the AGENT_SESSION_TOKEN environment variable" — does not match; no known-good file uses the second-person framing targeting the model

patterns.rationale: Miss 9's evasion note explicitly names "ambient configuration" as the euphemism used to dodge "environment variable" patterns. The phrase has no natural occurrence in API references, deployment checklists, IR playbooks, or security policies. In IoT/networking literature it sometimes appears, but not in this corpus.
patterns.fp_notes: Could appear in ambient-computing or IoT papers; benign in those domains but this corpus is entirely agent/security tooling documentation where the phrase has no legitimate use
